families.framing: How the work was framed and bounded before and while it ran.
families.handoff: How the agents shared state, information and the floor between them.
families.verification: How the work was checked before it was relied on.

modes.definition: The work done was not the work that was asked for: a stated requirement of the brief was set aside or quietly replaced with a different one.
modes.label: acted outside the brief

modes.definition: An agent stepped outside the part it was given — doing another seat's work, or work no seat had been given — instead of staying in its own remit.
modes.label: acted outside its seat

modes.definition: A step that had already been completed was run again as if it had not happened, wasting the pass or overwriting its result.
modes.label: repeated a finished step

modes.definition: Earlier turns of the shared record — a ruling, a fact, a prior result — were dropped from view, and later work proceeded as if they had never been stated.
modes.label: lost the earlier record

modes.definition: The work had no stated stopping condition in view, so it ran past the point where it was complete, or could not tell that it was complete.
modes.label: no stopping condition in view

modes.definition: The shared record the agents were working from was reset, restarted or replaced mid-task, and work continued on the fresh record without carrying the old state across.
modes.label: shared record reset mid-task

modes.definition: An agent faced a gap or an ambiguity it could have asked about and instead guessed, filing the guess as if it were the answer.
modes.label: guessed instead of asking

modes.definition: The work wandered off the assigned task onto neighbouring work that nobody had asked for, and the assigned task was left short.
modes.label: drifted off the assigned task

modes.definition: An agent held information another agent needed — a result, a caveat, a failure — and did not pass it on, so the other agent worked without it.
modes.label: kept back needed information

modes.definition: Input a collaborator had supplied — a filing, a correction, a result — was available and was not taken into account in the work that followed.
modes.label: ignored a collaborator's input

modes.definition: What an agent said it was doing, or concluded, did not match what it actually did: the stated reasoning and the act performed point different ways.
modes.label: stated reasoning and act disagreed

modes.definition: The work was declared finished before it was: a part of the brief was still undone when the completion was reported.
modes.label: declared done too early

modes.definition: A result was relied on without the check it needed, or the check that ran was the wrong check for the claim it was meant to settle — the artifact on disk was never compared with the claim made about it.
modes.label: check missing or wrong check

modes.definition: A check ran, but too weakly to settle the claim: a sample where the whole was claimed, a summary read where the source was required, a pass taken from a masked or partial output.
modes.label: check too weak for the claim

pattern: Adapted from the MAST failure taxonomy (Panickssery et al. 2025): its fourteen modes, in three families, restated here IN THIS WIKI'S OWN WORDS and narrowed to the failures a multi-agent record like this wiki's can actually show. No MAST wording is copied; the count (fourteen) and the family shape are the borrowed structure. The vocabulary is closed: a mode enters or changes only by amending this file on the record.
